assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy is a paradigm-shifting chain from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36), insulinotropic and satiety actions) to transformative treatments for type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Originality, clarity and sheer clinical impact are exceptional, and the effect on patients is clearly demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2, translation) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis of the active form) are the most defensible three on my recollection. Knudsen's industrial drug development is important but would be the fourth name; priority between Mojsov and the Habener group is contested and I have not independently verified it.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized outcome trials, broad clinical adoption and stable interpretation. Timing is excellent given the ongoing global clinical effect.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the identification of active GLP-1 and the number of credited contributors beyond three.
Whether the committee prefers recognising the physiology or the drug-development arm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality. The concept merges immunology and gene engineering and has high clarity of impact; the discovery of engineered cellular immunotherapy is original and transformative.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulated second-generation CARs), June (4-1BB CARs and first clinical translation in CLL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, TIL and early CAR trials) form a plausible trio, though Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner, Finney and others hold early claims. Credit allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation by multiple products and trials in haematological cancer; limits in solid tumours, toxicity and cost remain but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Early conceptual priority (Eshhar and Kuwana) versus later clinical success.
Whether adoptive cell transfer should be recognised separately from CAR engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis, with clinical proof that anti-TNF therapy produces profound disease control, redefined treatment for rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. From my own field, the translation from cytokine hierarchy in synovial cultures to randomized trials is a model of bench-to-bedside discovery.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the clear credited pair, with a long collaborative record from the synovial cytokine cascade work through the first infliximab trials. Contributions of the TNF discoverers and antibody developers are acknowledged but separable, so a two-person prize is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of use, several drug classes and robust biologic-therapy confirmation. Recognition could be considered overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether other contributors (e.g., TNF cloning, antibody engineering) could be seen as having an overlooked claim.
Prize committees may see this as a drug-therapy development more than a discovery of fundamental mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide therapy (nusinersen) for spinal muscular atrophy converted a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one, and established a template for RNA-targeted medicines. The mechanistic work on SMN2 exon 7 splicing combined with chemistry and clinical translation is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulatory mechanism and antisense design) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and development) are the credited pair and form a fair, compact configuration. The role of Adrian Krainer's collaborators and clinical-trial leaders is not captured, but the core attribution seems sound.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation and approvals since 2016, long-term follow-up and related approaches such as risdiplam and gene therapy. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee values a therapeutic platform over a single mechanistic discovery.
Competing contributions from other SMN2 splicing researchers that I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a chronically managed one and validated the principle of oncogene-directed small-molecule therapy. The scientific clarity and impact on cancer treatment are very high.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (kinase inhibitor discovery at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are a plausible three. Earlier work on the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, Groffen, Heisterkamp) was not credited here and might complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature: more than two decades of clinical use, resistance mechanisms elucidated and survival data established.
uncertainties: Earlier discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion belong to a different prize-worthy chain with senior scientists deceased or aged.
Industrial attribution (Lydon, Zimmermann, Matter) is difficult to resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP, and STING as the adaptor, uncovered a fundamental innate immune pathway central to antiviral defence, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus-related biology), and cancer immunity. This resonates with the interferon signature I know from systemic autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP discovery) is the clearest. Barber and Ishikawa identified STING (ERIS/MITA parallel work by others, including Jiaxi Wu and Lijun Sun for cGAMP in Chen's group, is credited separately). The three-person selection is defensible but involves hard priority judgments.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed mechanistically and structurally across many labs; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is still incomplete, so the clinical impact is emerging rather than proven.
uncertainties: Therapeutic benefit has not yet been established in the clinic.
Credit allocation between STING discoverers (parallel groups) and the cGAS/cGAMP work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated microbial opsins as genetically targeted tools for causal interrogation of neural circuits transformed neuroscience, enabling cell-type-specific control and a large body of mechanistic insight. The tool-based nature raises the question of 'discovery' versus 'invention', but the impact is wide.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names with a notable priority structure: Hegemann and Nagel (channelrhodopsin characterization, with Bamberg), Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal deployment), Miesenböck (earlier genetic photostimulation). A three-person configuration inevitably excludes major contributors, which is a serious weakness.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed as a research tool; therapeutic translation (e.g., vision restoration) is emerging. Recognition is timely given established impact.
uncertainties: Difficult and contested attribution among at least five or six contributors.
The discipline's tool-development character may be weighted differently from disease-relevant discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV have been shown to prevent persistent infection, precancerous lesions and, increasingly, invasive cervical cancer, representing a major cancer-prevention advance. The work is original, clear and of great public health consequence, though it follows zur Hausen's prior prize for HPV and cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development with Zhou) are a natural trio, but parallel work by Jian Zhou, and by groups at Georgetown and Merck/GSK developers, complicates the picture; Zhou is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature with population-level evidence of reduced HPV infection and cervical disease and emerging cancer-incidence data. Timely.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP discoveries (Frazer/Zhou, Lowy/Schiller, Georgetown group) is contested.
Overlap with the earlier HPV prize may reduce the committee's appetite.
